scene.note: The same page has to read well on a monitor and on a phone. You tell phones their real width and let sizes and layout follow the screen.

steps.note: Kofi's phone lays the page out for a wide screen, then shrinks it to a tiny copy.
A line in the head of each page tells the phone to use its own width, at normal size.
The phone lays the page out at its real width, and the words are big enough to read.
The studio picture is wider than a phone, so it runs off the edge.
Each picture may be narrower than its own size, never wider than its box, and keeps its shape.
On a phone the picture fits the screen. On a monitor it keeps its own size.
Some readers set larger text on their phone. A size in px ignores them.
The body's text size is written in rem, measured against the reader's own setting.
The page looks the same as before, and grows for readers who asked for larger text.
The content of the page has one fixed width, wider than any phone.
The fixed width becomes an upper limit in rem: wide screens stop there, narrow ones go below it.
On a monitor the lines stay short enough to read. On a phone the content is as wide as the screen.
On a phone the two class cards are squeezed side by side.
A media query changes the columns of the classes, only on screens below Kofi's breakpoint.
On a phone one card sits above the other. On a wider screen they stay side by side.
